title: useEffect Hook with Empty Dependency Array
options: It will execute after every re-render
It will execute only once after the component mounts
It will execute before component unmounts
explanation: Passing an empty dependency array `[]` tells React that the effect function does not depend on any props or state values, so it runs only once after the initial render (mount).

explanation: When `props.visible` changes to true, the effect triggers and logs 'Hello' once. Calling `setCount(1)` triggers a re-render. Since `props.visible` did not change during the second render, the effect does NOT fire again.

title: Conditional JSX Unmounting
options: MyChild is unmounted when value is not 3
MyChild re-renders on every prop update without unmounting
explanation: In React, when a conditional expression evaluates to `false`, React unmounts the component tree for that element and destroys its internal state and ref hooks.

title: Accessing Context Values in Functional Components
explanation: `React.useContext(Context)` accepts a context object created by `React.createContext()` and returns the current context value for that context from the nearest `<Context.Provider>`.

title: Uncontrolled Checkbox Input with useRef
options: inputRef.current.checked returns true/false reflecting actual DOM state
defaultChecked causes a runtime error with useRef
React converts it automatically to a controlled input
explanation: Using `defaultChecked` creates an uncontrolled checkbox component. Attaching a ref via `useRef` allows reading the native DOM property `inputRef.current.checked` directly.

title: Mutating Local Variables in Event Handlers
explanation: Mutating a plain local variable inside an event handler updates its value in the handler scope and logs 2, but does NOT trigger a React re-render. When the component re-renders later for another reason, `count` resets to 1.

title: Accessing Input Value via useRef
explanation: `inputRef.current` points to the underlying HTMLInputElement node. Dereferencing `.value` retrieves the current text value ('hello').

title: Rotate Array (Children's Game Simulation)
options: Rotate right by (k % n) positions using modulo indexing
explanation: Shifting elements to the right by k positions in a circular array requires calculating `newIndex = (i + k) % n`. Using modulo handles k > n and circular wrap-around efficiently in O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Queue FIFO Deletion Operations
explanation: A Queue operates on First-In, First-Out (FIFO). The first 3 enqueued elements (30, 70, 30) are deleted first, leaving [80, 50] in the queue.

title: Binary Search Tree Construction Validity
explanation: Binary Search Trees require elements to have a strict total ordering (comparable keys). Mixing numbers with mathematical symbol strings (`+`, `/`) breaks ordering guarantees unless custom comparators are defined.

title: React Render Props & Array Join Output
explanation: `render()` returns `['One', 'Two']`. Calling `Array.prototype.join()` without parameters defaults to a comma separator, producing string `'One,Two'`, rendered directly as visible JSX text.

title: React HOC Prop Forwarding via JSX Spread
explanation: Higher-Order Components pass props down to wrapped components. Using JSX spread `<div {...p}>` ensures all passed props (`onMouseEnter`, `style`) are attached to the underlying DOM node.

title: Minimum Removals to Change MEX Value (updateMEX)
explanation: To alter the MEX value of an array, you must remove all occurrences of at least one number less than MEX. Among values 0 and 1, number 0 has frequency 1, requiring 1 removal.

Statement 2: Efficient employees blindly accept any assigned task without questioning.
explanation: Statement 1 requires evaluating task value and applying wisdom, whereas Statement 2 advocates blindly accepting tasks without question. These statements directly contradict each other.

title: Critical Thinking — Customer Satisfaction & User Adoption Assumption

Conclusion: Early customer feedback enhances user adoption.

Costs of early customer involvement are offset by revenue.
Increased customer satisfaction results in increased user adoption.
explanation: The conclusion leaps from 'higher customer satisfaction' to 'enhanced user adoption'. For this argument to hold, it must assume that higher satisfaction leads directly to higher user adoption.

title: Deductive Syllogism — Manager and Team Leader Permissions
code:
Premise 1: All managers can view confidential documents.
Premise 2: All team leaders are managers.

No team leaders can view confidential documents.
explanation: Set inclusion: Team Leaders subset of Managers, and Managers subset of Confidential Document Viewers. Transitivity implies all Team Leaders can view confidential documents.
